recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Any future finer-grained profile-family constraint work should come from a new work-group decision rather than altering the already-applied FHIR-7796 rule.
issue_request: FHIR-7796 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 request for a convenient way to constrain Resource(Any) in profiles. The accepted resolution allowed a profile to reference an implementation guide as a profile on a reference type, with finer control left for post-DSTU2 exploration.
initial_application: Jira comments record svn revision 6109. Git commit a0b0f17cd40a206443ba821ed846ff680ed217e4 maps that application and changed source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml so ElementDefinition.type.profile could reference an implementation guide and require conformance to at least one profile defined in that guide.
additional_context: FHIR-7795 is the same change family and documents the implementation-guide/default-profile mechanism behind the resolution. Current source/fhir.ini keeps ElementDefinition active, current ElementDefinition source has canonical(StructureDefinition|ImplementationGuide) for both type.profile and the later type.targetProfile split, and ImplementationGuide.global/default profile source remains present. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-7796 found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current active specification already states the requested ImplementationGuide-as-profile behavior for datatype/resource profiles and reference target profiles.

related_jiras.note: Companion Published issue about avoiding profile fan-out through implementation-guide default profiles; it explains the mechanism cited by the FHIR-7796 comments but was not separately decided here.
